title: Renew the gateway's certificate without breaking handshakes

blocks.text: The API gateway terminates TLS. When its certificate is renewed, a reload thread reads the new certificate and private key from the secrets vault and the listener starts presenting them, without a restart. Since the last renewal, monitoring has shown a short burst of failed handshakes at every reload: clients received a certificate that the server's signature didn't match. Both fields in `TlsCredentials` are already `volatile`.

items: `reload(...)`: read the renewed certificate and key from the source and start using them;
`current()`: the certificate and key a new handshake uses.

blocks.text: When you're done, every handshake gets a certificate with the key that belongs to it, whenever it starts, and a handshake never waits for a reload, however slow the vault is. You may change how the credentials are stored. About five lines in total.
The tests hold the reload while it reads one part from the vault and start a handshake meanwhile.

cases.says: after each reload, a new handshake gets the certificate and key that reload read
a handshake that starts after the reload has read the new certificate but before it has read the new key gets the old certificate with the old key
a handshake that starts before the reload has read anything gets the old pair, never an empty or half-filled one
a handshake gets its credentials at once while a reload is still reading the source

origin.section: volatile Covers One Field: Values That Must Agree Are Swapped as One Immutable Object

concepts: Values that must agree go into one immutable object, built completely and published by one volatile write; two volatile fields let a reader see a new value with an old one.
